findings.summary: Lite leak (K1, confirmed): in Lite, `data-sorts-rules="<handle>"` inside `{% apply sorts %}`, `|raw|sorts`, a Markup value or `engine->apply()` turns on any built-in Pro rule (fractions, ranges, multiplication, ordinals, symbols, hook-amp, hook-caps). SPEC §2 makes every §3 rule beyond the Lite set Pro.
findings.location: src/engine/Engine.php:376 (`|| isset($scoped[$handle])` overrides the Lite options’ `false`); src/services/EngineService.php:100-110 (Lite expresses its limit as rule switches, which a scope overrides); docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:238 (documents `data-sorts*` as working wherever the engine runs)
findings.cause: Lite is enforced by switching rules off in Options, but the engine treats a data-sorts-rules scope as an independent way to turn any registered rule on. The built-in Pro rules are still registered in the Lite engine.

{% endapply %}` prints `½ cup, pages 1–5, 3×4, 1st place, A&B NASA © 10 kg`; `{{ s|raw|sorts }}` with `1/2 (c)` → `½ ©`; `sorts()->engine->apply('

1/2

')` → `½`. (CKEditor strips the attribute from stored content, so the leak needs template markup.)
findings.acceptance: In Lite no rule outside EngineService::LITE_RULES can run by any scope (give the engine an allow-list, or register only the Lite rules in the Lite engine). twig-test gains, for Lite: the apply-block above prints `1/2 cup, pages 1-5, 3x4, 1st place, A&B NASA (c) 10 kg` unchanged apart from Lite rules; for Pro the same block still converts. findings.summary: No size cap, and memory grows to 50–90× the page (K4, measured): a tag-dense page of a few MB exhausts a normal memory_limit inside the pass. That is a PHP fatal, which PagePass’s catch (Throwable) cannot catch, so the page 500s. The README promises “It never breaks a page.”
findings.location: src/engine/Engine.php:167 (preg_match_all with 11 capture groups, PREG_PATTERN_ORDER: 11 arrays of N entries); src/engine/Engine.php:188 (a 6-element segment array per text token, all held in one flow when the tags are inline); src/services/PagePass.php:37-45 (no size check); README.md:81
findings.cause: The whole page is materialised as token arrays before the walk, with no limit on page size or token count.
findings.repro: Host PHP 8.5.12, one apply(), `/opt/homebrew/bin/php -d memory_limit=-1 /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-dgaidula-sw-github-public-craft-sorts/00a5e988-4909-468c-bf8c-c01c1c5d14d6/scratchpad/gate-r7m3/k4.php `: product table rows 1 MB 163 ms +64 MB, 2 MB 328 ms +127 MB, 5 MB 835 ms +269 MB, 10 MB 1.68 s +537 MB; a run of a 1 MB 107 ms +90 MB, 2 MB 221 ms +180 MB, 5 MB 588 ms +576 MB; prose article 10 MB 399 ms +145 MB. In the testbed (PHP 8.4), `cd ~/sw/github-private/craft5-plugin-testbed && ddev craft shell < /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-dgaidula-sw-github-public-craft-sorts/00a5e988-4909-468c-bf8c-c01c1c5d14d6/scratchpad/gate-r7m3/k4craft.php` (PagePass::fix on a 6 MB table page at memory_limit=256M): "PHP Fatal Error 'yii\base\ErrorException' with message 'Allowed memory size of 268435456 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 2097152 bytes)' in /var/www/html/plugins/craft-sorts/src/engine/Engine.php:167"; a 3 MB table peaks at 154 MB.
findings.acceptance: The pass has a bounded cost. Either a cap (a page or token count over a documented limit, default no higher than about 2 MB, is sent as rendered with one Craft::warning naming the size), or tokenizing with memory a small multiple of the page (no 11-array PREG_PATTERN_ORDER result; walk with preg_match and an offset, or one capture group). A test renders a 6 MB tag-dense page through PagePass at memory_limit=256M and gets the page back (unchanged or converted) with no fatal. README "Performance" states peak memory per MB and the cap.

lang scoping (nearest ancestor, data-sorts-lang over lang, de-AT → de, unknown → site), inline-transparent vs block boundaries, data-sorts="off" subtrees with a nested data-sorts="on" staying off, nested skip elements.
